$comment: Story frames for two-digit numbers (G2-506, Year pages O, 2026-11-13). The story bank (word-problems-levelset.json + frames.js) was written for numbers to 20: a child HAS, BUYS, SEES or LOSES the things. With 53 forks or 90 pencils that reads absurd (teacher review of the German and Swedish lessons, 2026-11-13), so the within-100 page tells only stories in which the things lie in a PLACE (a table, a box, a shelf, a basket): the bank's own place frames plus the frames below, each modelled on a place frame of its language (same slots: {n1} {n2} {noun} {name}, {Q} = how many, agreeing, in es / pt / it). Read by a native reader (2026-11-13). Only G2-506 reads this file: the published pages of the other story types keep their draw. After the native read: the question "how many are missing in the blue box" names the red box as the target in every language ("so that both boxes hold the same" has a second answer: move half the difference). `subChange` (2026-11-13, read by the bar-model pages only): the change story on a shelf in which somebody takes the things down; the bank's own shelf story lets them fall, which a teacher would not print for 45 things.
